source_text: ἱερῶν Γραμμάτων τῆς ὧδε λαμπρᾶς καὶ ἀξιαγάστου λατρείας ἀνατύπου τὰς γραφάς. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἔφη τοίνυν Θεὸς ἐν τῷ Λευϊτικῷ, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι πρὸς πάντας τοὺς ἐξ Ἰσραήλ· «Ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ὑμῶν ἐὰν προσαγάγῃ δῶρα τῷ Κυρίῳ, ἀπὸ τῶν κτηνῶν καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν βοῶν καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν προβάτων προσοίσετε τὰ δῶρα ὑμῶν· ἐὰν ὁλοκαύτωμα τὸ δῶρον αὐτοῦ, ἐκ τῶν βοῶν ἄρσεν ἄμωμον προσάξει, πρὸς τὴν θύραν τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου προσοίσει αὐτὸ δεκτὸν ἐναντίον Κυρίου, καὶ ἐπιθήσει τὴν χεῖρα ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν τοῦ καρπώματος δεκτὸν αὐτῷ, ἐξιλάσασθαι περὶ αὐτοῦ. Καὶ σφάξει τὸν μόσχον ἔναντι Κυρίου, καὶ προσοίσουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἀαρὼν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὸ αἷμα, καὶ προσχεοῦσι τὸ αἷμα ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον κύκλῳ τὸ ἐπὶ τῶν θυρῶν τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου· καὶ ἐκδείραντες τὸ ὁλοκαύτωμα, μελιοῦσιν αὐτὸ κατὰ μέλη, καὶ ἐπιθήσουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἀαρὼν οἱ ἱερεῖς πῦρ ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον, καὶ ἐπιστοιβάσουσι ξύλα ἐπὶ τὸ πῦρ· καὶ ἐπιστοιβάσουσιν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἀαρὼν οἱ ἱερεῖς τὰ διχοτομήματα, καὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν, καὶ τὸ στέαρ ἐπὶ τὰ ξύλα τὰ ἐπὶ τοῦ πυρὸς τοῦ ὄντος ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, τὰ δὲ ἐγκοίλια καὶ τοὺς πόδας πλυνοῦσιν ὕδατι, καὶ ἐπιθήσει ὁ ἱερεὺς τὰ πάντα ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον· κάρπωμά ἐστι, θυσία, ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας τῷ Κυρίῳ.» Ἆρ' οὐκ ἐναργὴς ὁ τύπος τῆς τῶν ἁγίων ζωῆς, καὶ οἰκειότητος ὁλοτελοῦς, τῆς πρὸς Θεὸν ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἁγιασμῷ; Μορφούμεθα γὰρ ὡς ἐν τοῖς ἡμέροις τῶν ζώων, μόσχῳ τε, φημὶ, καὶ προβάτῳ, κόσμῳ μὲν ἀποθνήσκοντες διὰ τοῦ τὴν σάρκα κατανεκροῦν, ἵνα Θεῷ ζήσωμεν διὰ τῆς εὐαγγελικῆς πολιτείας, ἀναβαίνοντες δὲ ὥσπερ εἰς θυσίαν τὴν πνευματικὴν ἀληθῶς καὶ εὐοσμοτάτην δι' Υἱοῦ τῷ Πατρί. Καὶ φέρε σοι πάλιν τὰ ἐφ' ἑκάστῳ λέγωμεν, ἰσχνοεποῦντες ὡς ἔνι. Δῶρον μὲν γὰρ ὥσπερ τι τῷ πάντων κρατοῦντι Θεῷ τὴν ἰδίαν ἕκαστος ἀνατίθησι ζωὴν, πλὴν ὡς ἑκάστῳ δίδοται, καὶ ὡς ἂν ἔχοι μέτρον. Ὁ μὲν γὰρ, οὕτως· ὁ δὲ, οὕτως, ἴδιον ἔχων ἐκ Θεοῦ χάρισμα, κατὰ τὴν τοῦ σοφωτάτου Παύλου φωνήν. Ἐν γὰρ τοῖς μεγέθεσι τῶν ζώων, ἤτοι ταῖς κατ' εἶδος διαφοραῖς, τὸ ἀνίσως τε καὶ ἀνομοίως ἔχον, κατ' ἰσχὺν τάχα που τὴν πνευματικὴν καὶ κατά γε τὴν τῆς διανοίας, πλαγίως ὑποσημαίνεται. Εἴτ' οὖν ὡς ἐν μόσχῳ μέγας εἴη τυχὸν, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἄγαν εὐσθενὴς, ἤγουν ὡς ἔν γε προβάτῳ τὸ μεῖον ἔχων, καὶ τοῦ τελείου κατόπιν ἰὼν, ἑαυτὸν εἰς δωροφορίαν προσκομίζει Θεῷ, καὶ τοῦτο εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα, τουτέστιν, εἰς ὁλόκληρον ἀφιέρωσιν, οὐ μεμερισμένην ἔχων πρὸς τὰ ἐν κόσμῳ τὴν ζωὴν, ἀλλ' ὅλην ἐξ ὅλου δεκτήν τε [καὶ] ἱερὰν τῷ Θεῷ. Τοιόσδε τις ἔστω τῆς θυσίας ὁ τρόπος· Ἄρσεν τε καὶ ἄμωμον ἔστω τὸ θῦμα, φησί. Σύμμορφοι γὰρ ἀεί πώς εἰσιν οἱ ἅγιοι τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὅς ἐστιν ἄρσην τε καὶ ἄμωμος ἀληθῶς, τοῦ μὲν ἄρσενος, τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν, τοῦ δὲ ἀμώμου, τὴν ὑπερφυᾶ καὶ ἀνυπέρβλητον ἁγιότητα καταγράφοντος. Εἷς γὰρ ἡμῶν καθηγητὴς καὶ πάναγνος ἀσυγκρίτως, ὁ Ἐμμανουήλ. Ἄλλως τε (χρῆναι γὰρ δεῖ[ν] κἀκεῖνο εἰπεῖν, καὶ οἰήσομαι δεῖν)
pass_a_gloss: [PALL. cont.] …from the sacred Writings (ἱερὰ Γράμματα) shape out (ἀνατυπόω, impv.) the drawings/outlines (γραφαί) of the worship (λατρεία) here, splendid (λαμπρός) and admirable (ἀξιάγαστος). CYR.: God said then in Leviticus, plainly to all from Israel [Leviticus 1:2–9 LXX]: a man of you if he brings gifts (δῶρα) to the Lord, from the livestock (κτήνη), from the oxen (βόες) and sheep (πρόβατα) you shall bring your gifts; if his gift a whole burnt offering (ὁλοκαύτωμα), from the oxen a male (ἄρσεν) unblemished (ἄμωμος) he shall bring, to the door of the tent of witness (σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου) he shall bring it acceptable (δεκτός) before the Lord; and he shall lay his hand on the head of the offering (κάρπωμα), acceptable for him, to make atonement (ἐξιλάσκομαι) for him; and he shall slaughter (σφάζω) the calf (μόσχος) before the Lord, and the sons of Aaron the priests shall bring the blood and pour it around (προσχέω) on the altar (θυσιαστήριον) at the doors of the tent; and having flayed (ἐκδέρω) the burnt offering, they shall cut it by limbs (μελίζω κατὰ μέλη); and the priests shall put fire on the altar and pile (ἐπιστοιβάζω) wood on the fire; and pile the halves/cut pieces (διχοτομήματα), the head and the fat (στέαρ) on the wood on the fire on the altar; the entrails (ἐγκοίλια) and the feet they shall wash with water; and the priest shall put all on the altar: it is an offering (κάρπωμα), a sacrifice, an odour of fragrance to the Lord. Is not the type (τύπος) vivid (ἐναργής) of the life of the saints and of complete (ὁλοτελής) kinship/belonging (οἰκειότης) toward God in spirit and sanctification? For we are formed/portrayed (μορφόομαι) as in the tame (ἥμερα) animals, calf and sheep, dying (ἀποθνῄσκω) to the world through putting the flesh to death (κατανεκρόω), so that we may live (ζάω) to God through the Gospel way of life (εὐαγγελικὴ πολιτεία), going up (ἀναβαίνω) as into the truly spiritual and most fragrant (εὐοσμότατος) sacrifice through the Son to the Father. Come, let us say again the details on each, speaking finely (ἰσχνοεπέω) as possible. Each dedicates (ἀνατίθημι) his own life as a gift to God who rules all, but as is given (δίδοται) to each and as he may have measure (μέτρον). One thus, another thus, having his own gift (χάρισμα) from God, according to the most wise Paul [1 Corinthians 7:7]. In the sizes (μεγέθη) of the animals, or differences by kind (εἶδος), the unequal (ἀνίσως) and unlike (ἀνομοίως) state is obliquely (πλαγίως) hinted (ὑποσημαίνω), perhaps in spiritual strength (ἰσχύς) and that of the mind (διάνοια). Whether great as in a calf and very strong (εὐσθενής), or having the less as in a sheep and coming behind (κατόπιν) the perfect (τέλειος), he brings (προσκομίζω) himself as gift-offering to God, and this as whole burnt offering, that is, whole (ὁλόκληρος) dedication (ἀφιέρωσις), not having life divided (μερίζω, perf. ptc.) toward things in the world, but whole from whole, acceptable and sacred to God. Let the manner of the sacrifice be such: let the victim (θῦμα) be male and unblemished, he says [Leviticus 1:3]. For the saints are always somehow conformed (σύμμορφοι) to Christ, who is truly male and unblemished, 'male' describing (καταγράφω) the leading/ruling quality (τὸ ἡγεμονικόν), 'unblemished' the supernatural (ὑπερφυής) and unsurpassable (ἀνυπέρβλητος) holiness. For one is our leader (καθηγητής), incomparably (ἀσυγκρίτως) all-pure (πάναγνος), Emmanuel [Matthew 23:10]. Otherwise too (for it is necessary to say that also, and I shall think it needful)… [runs into §4].
pass_b_english: Palladius: …sacred Scriptures, sketch out the outlines of this splendid and admirable worship.

Cyril: Well then, God said in Leviticus, and plainly to all those of Israel: ‘If any one of you brings gifts to the Lord, you shall bring your gifts from the livestock, from the cattle and from the sheep. If his gift is a whole burnt offering from the cattle, he shall bring a male without blemish; he shall bring it to the door of the tent of witness, acceptable before the Lord. And he shall lay his hand on the head of the offering, acceptable for him, to make atonement for him. And he shall slaughter the calf before the Lord, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall bring the blood and pour the blood on the altar all around, the altar that is at the doors of the tent of witness. And when they have flayed the whole burnt offering, they shall cut it up limb by limb; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall put fire on the altar and pile wood on the fire; and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall lay the cut pieces, the head and the fat on the wood that is on the fire upon the altar; but the entrails and the feet they shall wash with water, and the priest shall lay all of it on the altar. It is an offering, a sacrifice, a fragrant aroma to the Lord.’ (Leviticus 1:2–9) Is this not a clear type of the life of the saints, and of their complete closeness to God in spirit and sanctification? For we are pictured in the tame animals — the calf, I mean, and the sheep — dying to the world by putting the flesh to death, so that we may live to God through the Gospel way of life, and going up, as it were, as a sacrifice that is truly spiritual and most fragrant, offered through the Son to the Father. And come, let us go through each point again for you, as finely as we can.

For each one dedicates his own life as a kind of gift to God, who rules over all, but as it is given to each, and according to the measure he has. For one has his own gift from God in one way, and another in another, as the most wise Paul says (1 Corinthians 7:7). In the sizes of the animals, that is, in their differences of kind, the inequality and unlikeness among us — in spiritual strength, perhaps, and in strength of mind — is hinted at indirectly. So whether someone happens to be great, as in the calf, and very strong indeed, or has less, as in the sheep, and falls short of perfection, he brings himself to God as a gift, and that as a whole burnt offering, that is, as an entire dedication. He does not keep his life divided toward the things of the world, but keeps it whole and entire, acceptable and holy to God.

Let the manner of the sacrifice be such as this: ‘Let the victim be male and without blemish,’ it says (Leviticus 1:3). For the saints are always in some way conformed to Christ, who is truly male and without blemish: ‘male’ describes his power to lead, and ‘without blemish’ his holiness, which is beyond nature and cannot be surpassed. For we have one Leader, pure beyond all compare: Emmanuel (Matthew 23:10). In another sense too (for this too must be said, and I judge that it must)…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 16. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withdrawn English was not used for wording.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

PG 68.1013. Opens mid-sentence inside Palladius's request; ἀνατύπου is an imperative addressed to Cyril (Palladius asks him to sketch the outlines from Scripture), and γραφάς here means 'outlines, pictures' (with ἀνατύπου, 'shape out'), not 'Scriptures'. The long quotation is Leviticus 1:2–9 LXX, and the English follows Cyril's wording; in v. 9 his text has singular ὁ ἱερεύς ('the priest'), where printed LXX editions may read the plural οἱ ἱερεῖς. Κάρπωμα rendered 'offering' to keep it distinct from ὁλοκαύτωμα 'whole burnt offering'. Ἰσχνοεποῦντες ('speaking finely, in detail') given as 'as finely as we can'. 1 Corinthians 7:7 is quoted almost word for word (ἴδιον ἔχων ἐκ Θεοῦ χάρισμα, ὁ μὲν οὕτως, ὁ δὲ οὕτως). Τὸ ἡγεμονικόν, 'the ruling/leading quality', given as 'his power to lead'. Εἷς … καθηγητής follows Matthew 23:10 (εἷς γάρ ἐστιν ὑμῶν ὁ καθηγητής, ὁ Χριστός). Uncited possible echoes, left without citation as doubtful: 'die to the world … so that we may live to God' (compare Galatians 2:19; Romans 6:11); 'as it is given to each … measure' (compare Romans 12:3; Ephesians 4:7); 'not divided' (compare 1 Corinthians 7:33–34); 'acceptable and holy' (compare Romans 12:1); σύμμορφοι (compare Romans 8:29). Editorial brackets in the source: δεῖ[ν] and [καὶ] (ἱερὰν) are printed as supplied; the English follows the supplied text. The sentence beginning Ἄλλως τε runs into §4.
